text:
maria: Heads up — since ~03:00 UTC we've seen a slow but steady rise in write latencies on the local-ssd pool in us-west-2. GPU provisioning starts failing with kube evict/attach timeouts. Attaching snippets below.

aj: Ugh. Any SMART or iostat yet?

maria: iostat shows per-disk util creeping to 99% on nodes with heavy batching, and write_qdepth growing. nvme SMART shows increased media errors on 3 drives in the same rack.

simon: Can you paste the iostat output?

maria: ```
Device            r/s     w/s     rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s wrqm/s  r_await w_await  aqu-sz  %util
nvme0n1         12.00  980.00   512.00 24576.00   0.00   0.00    0.21   18.74   1.85  97.60
nvme1n1         10.00 1020.00   256.00 24960.00   0.00   0.00    0.19   20.10   2.01  98.10
```

maria: and nvme-cli: ```
NVME SMART/Health Information for nvme0n1:
 critical_warning: 0
 media_errors: 124
 error_count: 127
 temperature: 42 C
```

aj: 124 media_errors is... not great. Those drives are probably in early wear-out or a firmware bug is surfacing. Which kernel dmesg lines?

maria: ```
[  612.345678] nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 2 timeout, resetting controller
[  612.346001] ata1.00: exception Emask 0x10 SAct 0x0 SErr 0x0 action 0x6
[  613.123456] nvme nvme0: aborting command
```

simon: Looks like intermittent controller resets. Could be thermal or a firmware path. Are these dedicated gpu nodes or mixed?

maria: Dedicated GPU nodes, running continuous batching for model infer. Load profile: long-running token streams, high synchronous tail.

ops-oncall: Currently 28 pods pending across 5 nodes — scheduler backlog. Rolling retries are killing throughput. We already started the ephemeral-cleaner on a few nodes but it's not enough.

aj: Short-term mitigation: 1) Reduce batch_max_tokens on the busiest routes to cut write amplification. 2) Triage the 3 bad drives by cordoning nodes and running `fio` verification before reboot. 3) Enable per-node KV cache eviction to reduce disk churn.

simon: Long-term: get a firmware rev from vendor or rotate to higher P/E-rated drives. Also update scrub schedule so it doesn't overlap peak GPU scheduling windows.

maria: Implementing (1) now — will route a canary traffic profile to 2 nodes. Reducing batch_max_tokens from 1024 -> 512 on heavy routes.

infra-bot: scrub-jobs@us-west-2 starting: node-gpu-117, node-gpu-118 (ID: #scrub-17455). ETA 18m.

maria: Can we avoid triggering full node scrubs at the same time? The cleaner seems to be running in parallel across the rack and might be amplifying writes.

aj: Good call. Simon, can you change cleaner concurrency? Right now it's configured cluster-wide to 10 parallel tasks. Drop to 3 for us-west-2 until we stabilize.

simon: On it. Changing config: `cleaner.max_parallel=3` for tag=us-west-2. Also will add a cooldown: `cleaner.cooldown_s=600`. Rolling that now.

maria: After reducing batch size and cleaner parallelism, observed immediate drop in write qdepth and %util -> 60-70% within 5m. GPU scheduling backlog decreased.

ops-oncall: Nice. Still seeing two nodes with persistent media_errors though. What's our replacement plan? Capacity impact?

aj: For replacements: we can 1) drain and reprovision with spare fleet nodes (cost: extra spot instances for ~48h), or 2) kick to Dedicated spare racks if available (higher cost). Prefer drain+replace from spare pool. Estimate: 8% capacity hit for 2 days, cost delta ~$1.2k/day.

maria: I'll open a reprovision ticket and tag infra-swap. Starting cordon/drain on node-gpu-117 to avoid mid-inference evictions.

infra-bot: node-gpu-117 cordoned by maria at 1745501360. Evictions started.

maria: Running targeted `fio` to confirm: ```
fio --name=write-test --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --size=1G --bs=256k --rw=write --iodepth=16 --numjobs=4 --time_based --runtime=60
```

maria: Results: write throughput sputters, errors increment. Confirmed failing.

aj: Ok pull that node from rotation, reprovision. Also schedule a firmware support ticket with vendor and attach SMART logs & dmesg. Ask for RMA on those drives if vendor confirms hardware.

simon: I updated deploy-runbook: if media_errors > 100 in 24h or controller resets >5 then auto-evict node and mark disk for RMA. We'll add a regen window to avoid mass-evicts during peak.

ops-oncall: For telemetry, can we add a tail-latency cost alarm? If local-ssd tail 99p > 25ms for 5m then alert SRE and optionally throttle non-critical routes.

aj: Agree — add alert and a policy: throttle PLG sample traffic to avoid billing blowouts. I'll propose thresholds in follow-up PR.

maria: Summary: mitigations applied (reduced batch size, lowered cleaner concurrency), cordoned 1 bad node and running reprovision, filing vendor ticket + RMA if they confirm. Observed immediate CPU/disk relief. Will follow up with detailed logs on the ticket.

simon: Thanks all. Once repaired, we'll run a controlled burn-in on spares before swapping to reduce early failures.

maria: tagging infra-swap, vendor-support, and ops for postmortem. :white_check_mark:

ops-oncall: Noted — monitoring closely for the next 6 hours.

infra-bot: scrub-jobs@us-west-2 completed on node-gpu-118 (duration 17m).

maria: last update: reprovision started for node-gpu-117 at 1745501500. Keeping channel open for next steps.
